battle.name: 西南戰爭
battle.theater: 熊本平原田原坂與鹿兒島城山
battle.brief: 一八七七年一月二十九日，鹿兒島私學校徒夜襲草牟田火藥庫奪取彈藥，二月十五日西鄉隆盛率一萬三千人出發西上，進抵熊本城下圍困鎮台。政府軍自博多與海路北上，雙方在高瀨與田原坂反覆爭奪；官軍以四斤山砲支援，三月二十日突破田原坂防線，四月解放熊本城，九月二十四日西鄉於城山自刃，此役遂終。

kit.name: 線膛砲
kit.history: 線膛讓同樣的藥量走得更遠。砲兵第一次可以在射程上贏步兵。

countries: 交戰的一方是明治政府。一八七七年二月十九日頒下的勅語任命有棲川宮熾仁親王為鹿兒島縣逆徒征討總督，以陸軍中將山縣有朋、海軍中將川村純義為參軍，參謀部、會計部、軍醫部、砲兵部、輜重部、裁判所與電信掛各設專職，參謀部只九十九人，砲兵部二百三十七人，電信掛七十四人。兵源以徵兵制為骨幹：東京、大阪、名古屋、廣島等鎮台的常備兵團、警視廳派出的警視隊，以及臨時徵募巡查組成的新撰旅團，編為第一旅團（野津鎮雄）、第二旅團（三好重臣）、第三旅團（三浦梧樓）、別動第一旅團（高島鞆之助）、別動第二旅團（山田顯義）與以警視隊為主體的別動第三旅團；海軍由川村純義節制，負責護送、登陸與艦砲支援。另一方沒有國家，是一八七四年六月設立在鹿兒島城廄跡的私學校：它既是銃隊學校，也是砲隊學校，骨幹是舊薩摩藩士，另吸納熊本藩士、其他縣郡士族與舊福岡藩士。薩軍按大隊編制，設七個大隊，另有熊本隊（池邊吉十郎）、黨薩諸隊、飫肥隊、佐土原隊、高鍋隊等地方武裝，總兵力在二萬至三萬之間。雙方力量懸殊：政府軍在八個月裡先後調動的兵力遠多於薩軍，但薩軍握有制式步槍的實彈與熟悉的地形，佔盡地利。
countriesEn: One side was the Meiji government. An imperial order of 19 February 1877 appointed Prince Arisugawa Taruhito Governor-General for the Suppression of the Rebels in Kagoshima Prefecture, with Army Lieutenant-General Yamagata Aritomo and Navy Rear-Admiral Kawamura Kiyoyoshi as his assistants, behind which stood a full establishment of specialists: a staff section, a pay section, a medical section, an artillery section of 237 men, a transport section, a war court and a telegraph section of 74 men, with only ninety-nine men in the staff section itself. The soldiers came from the conscript garrisons of Tokyo, Osaka, Nagoya and Hiroshima, from the police detachments the Metropolitan Police sent into the field, and from the Shin-sentai brigade raised by temporary conscription of former constables; these were formed into the 1st Brigade under Nozu Shizuo, the 2nd Brigade under Miki Shigetomo, the 3rd Brigade under Miura Goryo, the 1st Independent Brigade under Takashima Takanosuke, the 2nd Independent Brigade under Yamada Akiyoshi, and the 3rd Independent Brigade, whose backbone was the police; the navy, under Kawamura, handled escort, landing and naval gunfire support. The other side had no state at all: it was the private school founded in June 1874 on the site of the former stables of Kagoshima Castle, which was at once a rifle school and an artillery school, built on a core of former Satsuma samurai and drawing in samurai of the Kumamoto domain, of other provinces and of the former Fukuoka domain. The Satsuma army was organised in battalions, seven of them, with additional local forces such as the Kumamoto detachment under Ikebe Kichijuro, the To-Satsuma bands, the Obi, Sadohara and Takahada bands, and numbered between twenty and thirty thousand men in all. The imbalance was extreme: the government mobilized far more troops over the eight months, but the rebels held the service ammunition for the rifles they carried and knew the ground intimately, and that gave them their advantage.
people: 西鄉隆盛是薩軍的盟主。一八七三年十月他辭去參議返鄉，隨行的鹿兒島出身官員軍人約六百人；起兵前夕他仍在小根占狩獵，聽聞彈藥庫被襲與暗殺謠傳才回城，二月十五日率本隊一萬三千人出發，九月二十四日清晨在城山自刃，由別府晉介介錯。私學校幹部中，篠原國幹、河野主一郎、高城七之丞等七人於一月三十日密商應對，桐野利秋二月二日自吉田村返鄉商議舉兵，池上四郎、淵邊群平、邊見十郎太先後赴小根占勸進；西鄉小兵衛在二月六日的作戰會議上主張先取長崎以保物資，遭否決，卻在高瀬之戰中陣亡於繁根木堤防；村田新八、永山彌一郎、平川惟一先後戰死，池邊吉十郎率熊本隊隨軍作戰。政府方面，明治天皇居中為大元帥，山縣有朋主持陸軍廳並提議出兵，川村純義於九月二十三日赴城山受降，谷干城任熊本鎮台司令官並拒絕讓路，樺山資紀以鎮台參謀長身分在二月二十日派出偵察隊，開出西南戰爭的第一砲；乃木希典以少佐代理連隊長身分在植木與木葉連遭挫敗，與倉知實在段山狙擊重傷，二月二十三日身故；江田國道少佐在吉次峠狙擊篠原國幹得手，卻在隨後的混戰中同陣歿，警視隊參謀長福原和勝在南關負傷後不治。
peopleEn: Saigo Takamori was the leader of the Satsuma army. In October 1873 he resigned his seat as a member of the Privy Council and went home, taking about six hundred officials and soldiers born in Kagoshima with him; on the eve of the rising he was still hunting at Konoe, and only returned when he heard of the seizure of the arsenal and the rumours of an assassination plot. On 15 February he marched out with the main body, thirteen thousand men, and on the morning of 24 September he cut his own throat at Shiroyama, with Beppu Shinsuke acting as his kaishakunin. Among the private school's leaders, Shinohara Kunitomo, Kawano Shuichiro, Takashige Shichinojo and four others met secretly on 30 January to decide on a response; Kirino Toshiaki came back from Yoshida village on 2 February to argue for the rising; Ikegami Shiro, Fuchibe Gumppei and Hemmi Jurota travelled in turn to Konoe to urge Saigo to act. Saigo Kobei had argued at the council of war on 6 February that Nagasaki should be seized first to secure supplies, was overruled, and was killed at the Funagomi embankment in the battle of Takase. Murata Shinpachi, Nagayama Yaiichiro and Hirakawa Korei were killed in turn, and Ikebe Kichijuro led the Kumamoto detachment alongside the rebel army. On the government side the emperor stood at the centre as supreme commander, Yamagata Aritomo ran the War Ministry and proposed the dispatch of troops, and Kawamura Kiyoyoshi came down to Shiroyama on 23 September to receive the surrender. Tani Tateki commanded the Kumamoto garrison and refused Saigo's request for free passage; Kabayama Shigenori, the garrison's chief of staff, sent out a reconnaissance party on the evening of 20 February, and that party fired the first shots of the war. Nogi Maresuke, acting regimental commander as a major, was beaten at Ueki and Konoha; Yokaura Tomomi, struck by a sniper on Tanzan, was wounded and died on 23 February; Egata Kunimichi, a major, killed Shinohara Kunitomo at Yoshitsuge Pass and was killed in the same melee; and Fukuhara Kazukatsu, chief of staff of the police detachment, was wounded at Nankan and died of it.
kits: 卡面上的線膛砲是一八五零年前後德國裝備的克虜伯式線膛前裝野戰砲。槍管內壁刻有螺旋膛線，同樣藥量的砲彈在膛內受阻更小、初速更高，因此射程與精度都勝過舊式滑膛青銅砲，砲兵第一次可以在射程上壓過步兵；普魯士自一八五零年起成建制採用這類砲並大量外銷，技術隨購置與仿製傳入日本。一八七七年真正開火的是新式後裝砲：官軍以四斤山砲為攻田原坂的關鍵，砲身逾二百公斤，須由大量兵員牽引方能翻越田原坂，而三池往還的坡道正在薩軍堡壘的射界之內，砲兵屢屢受阻；最後官軍在二之坂一帶設三座砲台、配置八門大砲，並以橫平山砲兵陣地為支撐射擊，才配合步兵打開缺口。炮兵編制龐大，近衛砲兵大隊、砲兵第一、第四、第六大隊與預備砲兵第一、第二、第三大隊分屬各鎮台，征討總督府另設砲兵部。官軍全役出動野戰砲五十四門，並自臺灣遠征收回加特林砲兩門，連同臼砲、榴彈、燒彈與木管附件一併送交。薩軍則以私學校的砲隊學校自建砲隊，圍攻熊本城時即有砲隊參與，其砲多為鹿兒島各廠與火藥庫繳獲的舊砲，射程與精度遠遜。步兵層面，薩軍多持前裝式步槍，全役用彈約三百萬發；官軍裝備後裝式史奈德步槍，卻因鹿兒島屬廠的製造設備被搬走而斷了彈藥，屢次向海外購進空藥莢、向中國借調，並新蓋雷管製造所與鉛熔解爐，才補上缺口。
kitsEn: The gun on the card is a German Krupp-type rifled muzzle-loading field gun of about 1850. Its bore was cut with a spiral groove, so a shell fired with the same charge of powder met less resistance and left the barrel faster, giving it both range and accuracy over the old smooth-bore bronze pieces; artillery could for the first time outrange the infantry. Prussia fielded guns of this type in unit strength from 1850 and exported them widely, and the technology reached Japan through purchase and imitation. What actually fired in 1877 were the new breech-loaders. The government's key weapon was the four-shiki mountain gun: more than two hundred kilograms, it had to be hauled over Tabaruzaka by a large body of men, and the gradient of the Miike highway lay inside the firing arc of the rebel redoubts, so the guns were repeatedly held up. In the end the government established three gun positions with eight field guns near Nino-saka, and used the Yokohirayama artillery position as the base for the bombardment, and only then did the infantry break through. The artillery establishment was large: the Guards Artillery Battalion, the 1st, 4th and 6th Artillery Battalions and the 1st, 2nd and 3rd Reserve Artillery Battalions, distributed among the garrisons, with a further artillery section of 237 men on the Governor-General's staff. The government fielded fifty-four field guns over the whole campaign, and also recovered two Gatling guns from the Taiwan expedition, sending them on with their mortars, shrapnel and wooden mounts. The rebels built their own gun crews in the artillery school of the private school, and a battery took part in the siege of Kumamoto Castle; their pieces were mostly old guns seized in the Kagoshima factories and arsenals, far shorter in range and far less accurate. At infantry level the rebels carried mostly muzzle-loading rifles and used about three million rounds in all; the government, armed with breech-loading Snider rifles, was cut off from ammunition when the manufacturing plant of the Kagoshima arsenal was carried off, and only made good the shortage by buying empty cartridge cases overseas, borrowing from China, and building new fuse and lead-smelting facilities.
tactics: 薩軍打的是士族游擊與野戰結合的路數：以大隊為作戰單位，卻避免與政府軍主力正面決戰，專走山道、溪谷與村落之間，設邀線、埋伏、斷糧與襲擊，士官與隊長多由當地嚮導引路，打完即散回山村，藉耗散而非殲滅消耗對方兵力；田原坂一線則以切穿尾根的坡道與層層堡壘構成防線，砲位與步槍交錯成十字火網，縱深再配置高鍋、佐土原等後備隊，準備逐次消耗來犯之師。官軍以旅團作戰，沿三池往還、豐前街道、吉次往還三條路施壓，先用砲兵封住坡道兩側，再用大隊密集攻擊堡壘；三月十三日從植木口警視隊中抽出劍術優良者組成拔刀隊，以拔刀衝鋒對付堡壘守軍，第二次拔刀隊五十人投入橫平山之戰，僅二人無傷。三月二十日總攻，十九個中隊冒豪雨濃霧自二俁越谷逼近，砲兵自橫平山射擊，突擊直指薩軍出張本營七本，一擊而潰，薩軍各隊連鎖敗走。補給線上，政府軍以小倉、博多為基地，經海路把糧秣送至八代與熊本，海軍的登陸與艦砲直接左右戰局；薩軍靠鄉村徵集與繳獲維生，槍彈不足自三月即已顯現，最終因彈盡與飢疲而崩解。
tacticsEn: The Satsuma army fought a combination of samurai guerrilla war and set-piece action. Battalions were its tactical unit, yet it avoided pitched battle with the main body of the government army: it moved along mountain paths, streams and between villages, laying ambush lines, cutting roads and supply lines, striking and scattering again, with officers and captains guided by local men and local knowledge, wearing the enemy down rather than destroying him. Along Tabaruzaka, by contrast, it built a defensive line of cut paths following the ridges and of successive redoubts, with gun positions and rifles interlocking into crossfire, and with reserves such as the Takahada and Sadohara bands deployed in depth to consume the attacking force in stages. The government fought in brigades, pressing along three roads, the Miike highway, the Buzen highway and the Yoshitsuge highway; it used artillery to seal both flanks of the slope and then fed battalions into the redoubts. On 13 March it picked the best swordsmen out of the 354 men of the Uekiguchi police detachment and formed a sabre detachment to assault the redoubts with the sword; the second sabre detachment, fifty men strong, was committed at Yokohirayama and only two came through unharmed. On 20 March came the general assault: nineteen companies crossed the valley from Futamata in torrential rain and thick fog, the guns opened up from Yokohirayama, the thrust went straight for Shichihon where the rebel advanced headquarters stood, and the rebel line collapsed at a single stroke, each unit breaking in turn. On the supply line the government used Kurume and Hakata as bases and moved food and ammunition by sea to Yatsushiro and Kumamoto, so that the naval landing and naval gunfire shaped the campaign directly; the rebels lived off the villages and on captured stores, and their shortage of rifle ammunition was already visible in March, so that the army finally disintegrated from want of ammunition and food.
data: 時間由一八七七年一月二十九日私學校徒夜襲草牟田火藥庫起，至九月二十四日城山陷落止，前後約八個月。兵力方面，政府軍先後調動的數字在各家統計中差距甚大，概括說在六萬至十萬之間，薩軍則為二萬至三萬人；日方一般引用的戰死數為政府軍約六千四百人、薩軍約六千八百人，雙方從未共同核對。二月二十一日至二十二日攻擊熊本城時，薩軍出動約一萬四千人，熊本鎮台守軍約四千人。田原坂一線，薩軍最終部署薩軍三十小隊、熊本隊八小隊、佐土原隊與高鍋隊，總計約七千人。官軍在田原方面的戰死，自三月四日起累計二千四百零一人，僅三月二十日一日即四百九十五人；薩軍參戰的三十小隊中，隊長戰死者達十一人。彈藥消耗最為驚人：官軍全役用去步槍彈約三千五百萬發，三月田原坂一線平均每日三十餘萬發、多時達六十萬發，折合每擊傷一名薩軍士兵約需二千發；而出動的野戰砲只有五十四門。財政上，政府用於此役的軍費約四千一百萬圓，相當於當年度稅收四千八百萬圓的八成半。警視隊一旅單獨陣亡八百七十八人。薩軍繳獲的彈藥約八萬四千發，全役總用彈約三百萬發。
dataEn: The war ran from the night of 29 January 1877, when the private school's men raided the Kusumuda arsenal, to the fall of Shiroyama on 24 September, about eight months. On numbers: the government's total mobilisation is put very differently by different authorities, roughly between sixty and a hundred thousand men, against twenty to thirty thousand for the rebels. The figures of dead usually quoted in Japan are about 6,400 for the government and 6,800 for the Satsuma army, and the two sides never counted them jointly. When the castle of Kumamoto was attacked on 21 and 22 February, the rebels committed about fourteen thousand men against roughly four thousand in the garrison. On the Tabaruzaka front the rebels finally deployed thirty rebel companies, eight Kumamoto companies and the Sadohara and Takahada bands, some seven thousand men in all. Government dead in the Tabaruzaka sector from 4 March onwards totalled 2,401 men, of whom 495 fell on 20 March alone; on the rebel side, of the thirty companies engaged, eleven of their captains were killed. Ammunition consumption was the most staggering figure: the government fired roughly thirty-five million rifle rounds during the campaign, at Tabaruzaka averaging more than 300,000 rounds a day and reaching 600,000, which works out at about two thousand rounds for every rebel soldier hit, while only fifty-four field guns were brought into action. Financially the government spent about 41 million yen on the war, close to five-sixths of the 48 million yen of tax revenue for that year. The police detachment alone lost 878 men. The rebels had seized some 84,000 rounds in the arsenal raids and used about three million rounds over the whole campaign.
cause: 起因要從明治政府改造士族下手說起。廢藩置縣之後，政府接手各藩欠債與士族俸祿，家祿支出佔歲出三成以上，於是借四民平等之名推行徵兵令、秩祿處分與廢刀令，舊士族的經濟基礎與身分特權一併被削去，士族反亂接連出現在佐賀、佐瀨、神風連與萩，九州士族的怨氣尤其集中在鹿兒島。引爆點是一八七七年一月二十九日夜私學校徒夜襲草牟田火藥庫奪取武器彈藥。導火索是陸軍省把鹿兒島屬廠的史奈德步槍彈藥製造設備秘密運往大阪；那座屬廠的前身是薩摩藩的大砲製造所，火藥與器械是藩士共同出資購置的，私學校徒認為中央來搬自家的財產，於是以守財產的名義動手。一月三十日篠原國幹等七名幹部聽聞中原尚雄一行返鄉是為了暗殺西鄉，二月三日更以酷刑逼出供述，說是大警視川路利良下的令，私學校徒群情激憤，至此舉兵已無退路。當時米價下跌、連年豐收，各地又先後出現農民一揆，士族的忿懣與民間的困苦混在一起。
causeEn: The origins lie in the Meiji government's attempt to remake the samurai class. After the abolition of the domains and the counties, the government inherited the debts of every domain and the obligation to pay samurai stipends, and the stipends alone took more than thirty per cent of state expenditure, so that under the slogan of equality among the four classes it pushed through the conscription ordinance of 1873, the commutation of stipends in 1876 and the edict abolishing the wearing of swords. The economic base and the privileged status of the old samurai were stripped away together, and samurai risings followed one after another at Saga, Sasebo, Shinkinkō and Hagi, with the anger of the Kyushu samurai concentrated above all in Kagoshima. The trigger was the night of 29 January 1877, when the private school's men raided the Kusumuda arsenal and seized arms and ammunition. The fuse was the War Ministry's removal, in secret, of the Snider ammunition machinery from the Kagoshima arsenal to Osaka. That arsenal had grown out of the Satsuma domain's own gun foundry, and the powder and machinery in it had been paid for by the samurai with money they had subscribed among themselves, so the private school's men held that the centre was coming to rob their own property, and struck first in the name of guarding it. On 30 January seven leaders including Shinohara Kunitomo learned that Nakahara Naao and his party had returned home to assassinate Saigo, and on 3 February, after torture, they extracted a statement saying that the Metropolitan Police Commissioner Kawaji Toshiyoshi had given the order. The private school's men were inflamed past the point of return, and there was no longer any way back from raising the standard. Rice was cheap because of good harvests, peasant risings were breaking out all over the country, and the anger of the samurai was mixed with the hardship of the countryside.
impact: 西南戰爭是日本最後一次內戰，制度上的收束比戰場勝負更深遠。士族作為軍事專門階層就此消滅，徵兵制與四民皆兵的國民軍隊取得無可置疑的地位，並證明以農民為骨幹的部隊足以戰勝由名門子弟組成、裝備與訓練俱佳的精銳義勇軍。警察的定位隨之轉向：警視廳一度改稱東京警視本署，以便合法派兵赴戰場，戰後退回日常治安，一八八一年恢復警視廳編制，定員由六千人減半，一半併入新設的東京憲兵隊；政府同時加緊收繳民間槍砲，翌年把一萬挺舊式前裝步槍回收入廠改造，以防內亂再起。財政上政府為此舉債，濫發不換紙幣，造成惡性通脹與通貨信用崩壞，四年後松方正義推行回收不換紙幣的松方通貨緊縮政策，確立兌換本位；伴隨而來的是小作化率由百分之三十八升到四十七、大地產集中與租佃糾紛增加，鐵道建設亦因財政拮据而由官營轉向民營。戰爭同時催生新的民間組織：五月佐野常民與大給恆設立博愛社，成為日本赤十字社的前身。軍歌拔刀隊與大量西南戰爭錦繪流傳，塑造了國民對這場戰爭的敘事。戰術層面的教訓最為刺眼：官軍以壓倒性兵力與火力卻長期攻不下田原坂，最後靠三月二十日的天候、集中砲火與拔刀隊才打開缺口，說明近代化軍隊並非只靠人數與後膛步槍就能解決地形與縱深防禦的問題。
impactEn: The Southwest War was the last civil war in Japanese history, and its institutional consequences went deeper than the result on the battlefield. The samurai as a distinct military profession ceased to exist, and the conscript national army built on the principle of all men as soldiers of the four classes took over an unchallenged position; the war also demonstrated that a force of conscript farmers could defeat a picked corps of gentlemen's sons with excellent arms and training. The role of the police was redefined accordingly: the Metropolitan Police was temporarily renamed the Tokyo Metropolitan Police Headquarters so that it could lawfully send detachments to the battlefield, and after the war it went back to ordinary public order; in 1881 the Metropolitan Police was restored with its establishment halved from six thousand, half of the men being transferred to the newly formed Tokyo military police, while the government tightened the collection of private firearms and in the following year took in ten thousand obsolete muzzle-loading rifles for conversion in the arsenal, so as to forestall another rising. Financially the government met the war with loans and a flood of inconvertible notes, producing runaway inflation and a collapse of credit in the currency; four years later Matsukata Masayoshi's policy of withdrawing the inconvertible notes, the Matsukata deflation, put the country on a gold standard, and it was accompanied by a rise in the rate of tenant farming from thirty-eight per cent to forty-seven per cent, by the concentration of landownership and by more disputes over tenancy, while railway construction, held back by the empty treasury, turned from state to private hands. The war also produced a new civilian organisation: in May Sano Tsunetami and Okyu Tsuneo founded the Hakuaisha, which became the Japan Red Cross Society. The military song Batōtai and the many woodblock prints of the war passed into circulation and shaped the national telling of the story. The tactical lesson is the most cutting of all: with overwhelming numbers and firepower the government could not take Tabaruzaka for weeks, and only the weather, concentrated gunfire and sabre detachments on 20 March opened the gap, showing that a modern army is not made whole by numbers and by the breech-loading rifle alone, when the ground and the depth of the defence are what matter.
result: 三月二十日官軍突破田原坂，薩軍在有明海、吉次、植木、隈府一線重整防線；海軍自長崎運兵、於八代登陸並北上，熊本城的長圍在四月十三日開始鬆動，四月十四日包圍解除，四月十五日全軍退出平原。四月十九日至二十日城東會戰薩軍再敗，本營退往人吉，六月一日人吉陷落；七月二十四日都城失守，七月三十一日放棄宮崎，八月十四日延岡為政府軍占領，八月十六日西鄉下令解散，黨薩諸隊相繼降伏，首謀者如石井貞興被判斬首。八月十八日西鄉率三百人（連軍夫共四百人）突破可愛岳的包圍網，九月一日突入城山立籠。九月二十三日河野主一郎與山野田一輔下山與川村參軍會見，傳達以當日下午五點為限的投降期限，西鄉只答一句：無須回覆。九月二十四日午前四時政府軍發動總攻，西鄉在前線肩腹中彈，當場自刃，由別府晉介拔刀介錯；午前七時岩崎口的堡壘陷落，殘部崩解，戰爭以政府軍的勝利告終。十二月末的大赦令赦免多數舊士族，私學校被解散，薩摩藩的藩主地位在明治政府接收名島的同時廢除；西鄉隆盛之死則成為日後追思與再評議的對象，而日本此後再無內戰。
resultEn: With the breakthrough at Tabaruzaka on 20 March, the rebels fell back and built a new line from the Ariake Sea through Yoshitsuge, Ueki and Kumafu. The navy carried troops by sea from Nagasaki, landed them at Yatsushiro and pushed north, and the siege of Kumamoto Castle loosened from 13 April, was broken on 14 April and the rebel army left the plain entirely on 15 April. The rebels lost again in the battle east of the castle on 19 and 20 April and moved their headquarters to Hitoyoshi, which fell on 1 June; Miyakonojo was lost on 24 July, Miyazaki was abandoned on 31 July, Nobeoka was occupied by government troops on 14 August, and on 16 August Saigo issued the order to dissolve, whereupon the To-Satsuma bands came in one after another and such leaders of the revolt as Ishii Sadayuki were sentenced to death by beheading. On 18 August Saigo with three hundred men, four hundred counting the baggage carriers, broke through the encirclement at Kai-dake, and on 1 September he stormed and fortified Shiroyama. On 23 September Kawano Shuichiro and Yamano Taichisuke came down the mountain and met Kawamura, who conveyed a deadline of five that afternoon; Saigo's answer was that no answer was needed. At four in the morning of 24 September the government launched its final assault; Saigo was shot through the shoulder and belly at the front and cut his own throat there, with Beppu Shinsuke giving him the coup de grâce by sword; at seven the redoubt at Iwasakiguchi fell, the remnants dissolved, and the war ended in a government victory. A general amnesty at the end of December pardoned most of the former samurai, the private school was dissolved, and the Satsuma domain lost its status as a feudal lord at the moment the Meiji government took over Noshima. Saigo's death became an object of later remembrance and reassessment, and Japan would have no further civil war.
